articles.title: To watch and watch for: Week of Nov. 15
articles.description: Fall recess is approaching, and whether or not you're celebrating Thanksgiving, the days off will be a much appreciated break from all our academic and professional obligations. If you find yourself looking for activities to fill the time, we've got plenty of recommendations for you. From novels to films to music, we have a wide range of selections to point you towards. We also have events for this week and the next - in case you're in Baltimore for the break! This year's Anora may be Jordan Firstman's Club Kid: an indie festival hit that has its theatrical release during break. The film follows Peter (Jordan Firstman), a New York club promoter with an accordingly whirlwind party-goer lifestyle, who deals with the sudden arrival of a ten-year-old kid he never knew he had. As he adjusts to newfound fatherhood, he also deals with the need to re-evaluate what his life should really entail. Club Kid and its understated but sincere charm will be the perfect watch for the Thanksgiving season as it questions what truly makes a family. The New York Times bestselling author T.J. Klune's newest mystery romance, Murmuration, will be a great cozy read. The novel is set in a seemingly idyllic small town that begins to slowly grow more odd. Mike, the protagonist, works his dream job at the local bookstore. He's ready to take the next step in his burgeoning romance with the small diner's waiter before he realizes the town they live in isn't quite what it seems. Murmuration's mystery will surely captivate any reader. The hotly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI releases on Friday, so maybe you're ready to spend the rest of your break with the video game of the year. Even if you're not a Grand Theft Auto fan, the game's accompanying album features new songs from some of the best working musical artists today. Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album already has singles from Young Lean, Metro Boomin, Future, Travis Scott, Morgan Wallen and Cardi B released ahead of the full album. PinkPantheress, Tame Impala and SZA are some of the other artists credited to appear on the tracklist. Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album's vast artist ensemble ensures that it will have something for everyone. During the upcoming break, the critically acclaimed The Wild Robot will be screening for free at The Walters Art Museum on Sunday, Nov. 22! The Wild Robot was nominated for the Best Animated Feature at the 2024 Academy Awards and it was widely praised in that year's award season. The film follows a sentient robot named Roz after she is shipwrecked and stranded on an island. Luckily, she manages to find a community in her harsh, unknown environment. The Wild Robot is a story about the importance of harmony with nature and those around you, and it makes for a moving watch this Thanksgiving season. As always, if you're looking for more activities to fill your time, we have a full list below: To watch… Club Kid, directed by Jordan Firstman - Nov. 26 All of a Sudden, directed by Ryusuke Hamaguchi - Nov. 25 Paper Tiger, directed by James Gray- Nov. 20 Minotaur, directed by Andrey Zvyagintsev - Nov. 20 The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, directed by Francis Lawrence- Nov. 20 To read… Murmuration, written by T.J. Klune - Nov. 17 Tiger's Mouth, written by Lucy Tan - Nov. 17 Nanny Nanny, written by K. Chiucarello - Nov. 17 Universe of Grace, written by Rachel Calnek-Sugin - Nov. 17 Deadlock, written by Chloe Gong - Nov. 17 To listen… Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album, by Various Artists - Nov. 19 Stargazer, by cikho - Nov. 20 Act 2, by Mother Soki - Nov. 20 Cute & Anxiety, by Yves - Nov. 20 SUIATSU, by Stray Kids - Nov. 25 Live Events… Sunday Screening: The Wild Robot - Nov. 22, 2-4 p.m. at The Walters Art Museum Registration is free and required. Andrea Chalupa presents A Reasonable Guide for Unreasonable Women - Nov. 19, 7-8:30 p.m. at Greedy Reads Registration is free and encouraged. Stars and Stripes: Artist Talk - Nov. 21, 2-4 p.m. at Galerie Myrtis Peabody Opera Theatre: "I due timidi" and "Gianni Schicchi" - Nov. 22, 3-6:30 p.m. at Miriam A. Friedberg Concert Hall, Peabody Institute This event is free. articles.title: Urban expansion causes ecological collapse in streams in the São Paulo Metropolitan Area
articles.description: The advance of urbanization in the São Paulo Metropolitan Area in Brazil is causing the collapse of food webs in local streams. A study published in August in the journal Nature Cities reveals that the impact of the metropolis goes far beyond a simple reduction in species. Degradation selectively eliminates organisms based on their size and simplifies ecological interactions. Networks of 190 connections plummet to just three.

articles.description: An elementary school watch party turned into a great opportunity to take a child’s-eye view of a spectacular astral phenomenon Maurice Bakley was chaperoning an eclipse watch party at his son’s elementary school in Arlington, Virginia, when he took this photograph. As he had arrived early to fit his iPhone to a tripod to capture a time-lapse of the event (with the help of a monocular and a solar filter), he reached for his iPad for this shot. “The boys in the photo, one of whom is my son, are part of a tight group of friends. They’ve known each other since kindergarten through their bilingual Spanish immersion school,” Bakley says. “They were eight and nine years old at the time, and none of them had ever seen an eclipse in real life.” Continue reading...
